title: One wallet, different promises
lines: Your wallet holds money that can buy lunch, money that expires, and promises you cannot freely transfer.
Money Was Never One Thing begins with that familiar collection, asking why we still speak as if money were singular.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Recognize monetary systems as varied institutions that distribute claims, trust and social opportunity.
emotionalPlan.visualActing: Keep several distinct forms of value in the wallet, showing their different usable contexts.
voiceDirections: Open with engaged, conversational curiosity; let the concrete situation carry the hook, with no ominous trailer voice.
Clear, interested and measured; emphasize the specific human stake, with no theatrical suspense.

title: Who makes a balance count?
lines: Bank deposits, cash, loyalty points, and platform credits carry different rules about who may use them.
Behind each balance sit decisions about issuing claims, extending credit, settling debts, and absorbing losses.

title: Money has a history
lines: The book follows monetary variety through history and institutional design, widening the questions beyond a favorite currency.
The ordinary act of paying becomes a way to notice how societies distribute trust and opportunity.
